title: VPC vs On-Prem Capacity Breakpoint Cheatsheet (spreadsheet + notes)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working reference + mini-spreadsheet schema for mapping where VPC (cloud-hosted customer VPC) makes more sense than on-prem appliances for customers, factoring licensing, support bundles, and capacity smoothing. This is not final — its a scratchpad to capture heuristics, example breakpoint math, and spreadsheet tab descriptions for the cost model well hand to Solutions Engineering.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- For sustained baseline steady-state inference demand under ~120 QPS equivalent on a single region with predictable growth, VPC usually wins on TCO when customers prefer OpEx and minimal ops headcount.
- On-prem becomes cost-advantaged if customers have large reserved capacity (>6–9 racks equivalent), strict data egress/sovereignty constraints, or if their discount/lease on HW reduces annualized infrastructure below ~40% of the hosted bill.
- Support & licensing bundles can flip the breakpoint: adding 24x7 Platinum support + on-site SLA pushes VPC breakpoint higher (i.e., on-prem becomes relatively more attractive).

Key assumptions used in examples below (annotated in spreadsheet):
- Model family: 32B dense-ish model, 8k context, optimized kernels available for both HW types.
- Token cost for hosted inference baseline (Redwood hosted): $0.0007 per token (placeholder for comparison).
- VPC cost includes: cloud GPUs, network egress, RDS-like control-plane (our managed pieces), and 3% overhead for storage + logs.
- On-prem cost amortized: HW capex (GPU price + chassis + networking) amortized over 4 years, plus ops headcount (FTEs), HW refresh tax, and power/cooling OPEX.
- Discounting: 8% WACC for NPV across multi-year scenarios.
- Utilization smoothing: if bursty workload, assume autoscaling inefficiencies: 20% additional capacity headroom for on-prem if ops conservative.

Quick formulas (to copy into sheet cells):
- Annualized Capex (USD/year) = (HW_purchase_price * (1 - residual_value_pct)) / amortization_years
- Effective unit cost per token (onprem) = (Annualized_Capex + Annual_Ops_Cost + Annual_Power_Network + Support_fee) / Annual_tokens_served
- Effective unit cost per token (vpc) = (Cloud_gpu_hourly * hours_per_year * avg_gpu_count + egress + managed_service_fee + support_fee) / Annual_tokens_served
- Breakeven_tokens_per_year = solve for tokens where cost_onprem == cost_vpc (sheet uses goal-seek)

Spreadsheet tabs (schema + columns) — planned for the shared sheet we hand to SEs: 
- input_parameters: short list of knobs (gpu_type, gpu_unit_cost, rack_gpu_count, amort_years, ops_fte_count, fte_cost, support_tier_pct, average_latency_sla, expected_qps_profile (CSV), avg_tokens_per_request)
- hw_cost_buildup: columns: item, unit_cost, quantity, total_cost, residual_value_pct, notes
- annualized_cashflow: year0_capex, year1_opex, year2_opex, discount_factor, npv, cumulative_npv
- utilization_profile: month, avg_qps, p95_qps, burst_factor, smoothing_policy, effective_gpu_hours_required
- support_licenses: tier, additive_fee_pct_of_base, includes_onsite, sla_hours, avg_response_time, recommended_customer_profile
- cost_comparison_output: scenario_name, annual_tokens, onprem_unit_cost, vpc_unit_cost, delta_pct, recommended_deployment, confidence_level
- scenario_bank: short narrative, bind_to_input_params_ref

Example scenario snapshots (numbers are deliberately approximate — use sheet for exacts):
Scenario A — mid-market chatbot (steady):
- Avg QPS: 30, avg tokens/request: 120, annual_tokens ~ 100B
- On-prem: Annualized capex (2x 8-GPU racks): $360k, ops 1.0 FTE ($160k fully loaded), infra opex $45k, support bundle 12% = $67k => effective unit cost ~ $0.0012/token
- VPC: managed GPU hours + egress + platform fee => unit cost ~ $0.0017/token
- Recommendation: On-prem preferred if customer can accept capex and ops; VPC if customer demands low up-front cost and rapid elasticity.

Scenario B — high-burst enterprise (bursty, unpredictable):
- Avg QPS: 8 but p95 bursts to 200, annual_tokens ~ 40B
- On-prem: needs big headroom or pre-warmed racks (inefficient); effective unit cost jumps due to low utilization (unit cost ~ $0.0025/token)
- VPC: can burst in region with reserved baseline + burst credits; effective unit cost ~ $0.0019/token
- Recommendation: VPC unless customer can commit to reserved on-prem patterns and accept low utilization inefficiencies.

Scenario C — ultra-regulated financial customer (data residency + long-term predictable loads):
- Avg QPS: 95, annual_tokens ~ 350B
- On-prem: amortized top-of-rack + on-site engineer + extended warranty => unit cost ~ $0.00085/token
- VPC: higher due to egress and managed fee => unit cost ~ $0.0011/token
- Recommendation: On-prem unless customer has strict policy against hardware on-site. Also note: heavy discounts on licensing or leasing change breakeven dramatically.

Heuristics & decision heuristics (one-line rules to put into Solutions Eng playbook):
- If annual_tokens < 20B and QPS < 10 avg -> VPC unless ops headcount already exists (opportunity to upsell support bundle).
- If annual_tokens between 20B–200B -> evaluate onprem if customer can take on capex and wants lower unit economics; otherwise VPC for faster time-to-value.
- If peak/p95/variance ratio > 6 -> prefer VPC because autoscaling inefficiency on-prem is expensive.
- If support requirements include on-site 24/7 + expedited RMA -> onprem support bundle adds ~8–15% to cost, factor into breakpoint.

Support bundle guidance (notes to include in pricing doc):
- Basic: remote support, ticket SLA 48h — baseline % fee 4–6% of annualized infra/service
- Standard: 8x5 phone, quicker escalations, 12% — default for most mid-market onprem deals
- Platinum: 24x7 + onsite spares + RPO/RTO commitments, 20%+; used for finance/healthcare enterprise deals
- For VPC customers add managed-monitoring fee (flat per-region + % usage) instead of onsite costs

Ops & implementation constraints (gotchas):
- GPU availability for on-prem SKUs: procurement lead time 12–20 weeks; factor into delivery SLA and possible bridging with VPC for first 6 months.
- Software lifecycle: customers often want pinned versions; support bundle must include upgrade windows and a rollback plan — cost this as engineering time (annually ~0.03 FTE per 100 GPUs).
- Power density & datacenter networking: some customers need >40kW racks -> add $20–40k per rack in facility prep (one-time).

Open questions / TODO (for follow-up with SE + Pricing):
- Validate real-world egress assumptions for top 10 customers (linked spreadsheet needs region-specific egress rates) — ACTION: Marco to pull last 12 months of traffic for customers with >50B tokens.
- Confirm discounting policy for multi-year reserved VPC commits vs on-prem amortization assumptions — ACTION: Finance to confirm WACC choice and tax treatment.
- Add a small sensitivity tab in the sheet that toggles only support-bundle level and shows new breakeven.

Quick implementation notes for sheet owner (Devon):
- Build input_parameters as first tab and lock formula tabs; color-code cells needing SE input (yellow). Keep a scenario_bank tab with copyable JSON-like param blocks for repeatability.
- Add a small chart (breakeven tokens vs support_pct) and a single row summary that the SE can paste into customer proposals (2 lines: recommended deployment + delta per token).

Short-term next steps (1–2 weeks):
- Build the sheet skeleton with tabs above and one completed example (Scenario A) — Devon
- Run the sheet with 3 live customer profiles from CS to sanity-check breakpoints — Aisha + Karen
- Draft two proposal snippets (on-prem proposal + VPC proposal) that include recommended support tiers and a simple migration/bridge plan (VPC-first -> on-prem later) — Marco

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep model family assumptions obvious in the sheet header; do not bake in "Redwood hosted token price" as canonical — it changes. Use it only for comparison.
- Customers often look at per-request latency more than per-token cost — add a one-liner about latency SLOs and their cost impact.

Linked refs (for later polishing):
- internal pricing compendium (confluence) — linked above
- SRE-runbook for on-prem installs (GH link in artifacts)
- legal-standard support terms (Karen to add)

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally informal — final model should be converted into a controlled Google Sheet and a polished one-pager for customers.
